drafts.title: PSE&G GridSmart $5k + $25k 0% on-bill
drafts.window: 8-11 AM MT (East Coast late morning still fine).
drafts.angle: PSE&G GridSmart (launched Aug 26, 2026): $5,000 instant rebate toward a qualifying home battery + up to $25,000 interest-free on-bill repayment. Pilot VPP: they may call the battery on peak events with advance notice. US lesson for everyone outside NJ: call your utility and ask for the battery cash + 0% on-bill twin before you pay retail.
bullets: PSE&G newsroom Aug 26, 2026: GridSmart Battery Program pilot for residential electric customers.
$5,000 incentive toward purchase and installation of a qualifying home battery; up to $25,000 interest-free on-bill repayment for remaining costs.
Rebate is applied as a contractor invoice credit (not a separate check). Participating contractor required. Enrollment capped.
During scheduled GridSmart events, battery covers part of the home load to cut peak draw. Advance notice. Backup during outages remains the household product.
Aligns with NJBPU push toward statewide VPP framework and NJ storage targets; pilot data feeds the bigger rulebook.
drafts.body:
New Jersey just made the battery invoice shorter.

PSE&G's GridSmart pilot will put $5,000 straight onto a qualifying home battery install. Then it will let you roll up to $25,000 of what is left onto the utility bill at 0% interest. That is not a blogger rumor. It is the Aug 26 utility press release and the program FAQ.

How it actually clears:

You use a participating contractor. The $5,000 shows up as a credit on that contractor's invoice. It is not a rebate check you chase for six months. Enrollment is limited. Approved hardware only. In exchange, PSE&G can call scheduled GridSmart events on peak days. Your battery covers part of the house so the neighborhood peak softens. They say you get notice ahead of time. When the grid dies, the battery is still your backup for lights and fridge.

If you do not live in PSE&G territory, do not shrug and scroll.

This is the national pattern to steal:

1) Upfront cash that cuts the sticker.
2) Cheap or 0% on-bill money for the rest.
3) A VPP or peak event in exchange.

Call your own utility and ask for those three by name. Ask whether a medical baseline or outage history bumps you. Ask whether solar is required. Get the answer in email.

Kitchen-table take for a 42-year-old with kids and a 62-year-old who hates the generator smell:

Backup is the product. The $5,000 and the 0% are how a normal household buys it without draining the emergency fund. The peak event is the membership fee. Read the hours. Keep a reserve for outages. Do not let a salesperson skip the event rules.

35-54 line: this is how you stop waiting for a federal credit that already expired.

55+ line: independence is a fridge that stays cold and a CPAP that stays on. Ask for the utility cash before you write the big check.

drafts.title: Used EVs >50% under $30k
drafts.angle: Recurrent Q3 2026 used-EV market: more than half of used EV inventory under $30,000; Cox data cited ~44% of used EVs sold in March under $25,000. Lease-return wave (~500k in 2026). Kitchen-table: buy battery health, not Facebook range anxiety.
bullets: Recurrent Used Electric Car Prices & Market Report (Q3 2026): more than half of used EV inventory under $30,000; deep off-lease supply (proprietary model: as many as ~500,000 lease returns in 2026, more in 2027).
Cox Automotive (via Recurrent): 44% of used EVs sold in March went for under $25,000.
Recurrent mid-year: average used EV values up ~5.1% Jan-Jun 2026 across matched model-year pairs; under-$20k segment up ~9.4% (demand at the cheap end).
Common under-$30k names in market explainers: Tesla Model 3 mid-$20ks; Chevy Bolt often under $20k; lightly used Ioniq 5 / Kona / Niro in the band when depreciation cooperates.
Federal used-EV tax credit expired Sep 30, 2025 in market explainers. State-of-health report matters more than a dead credit line.
drafts.body:
The used EV lot finally looks like a normal car lot.

Recurrent's 2026 used-EV report says more than half of the inventory sits under $30,000. Cox numbers they cite put 44% of March used-EV sales under $25,000. Lease returns are flooding in. Their model talks about roughly half a million lease returns this year and more next year. That is how a 2019-2023 EV stops being a rich-person leftover and starts being a family second car.

Prices at the cheap end even firmed up in the first half of 2026. Recurrent saw average used EV values up about 5.1% from January to June on matched cars. The under-$20,000 band jumped harder, about 9.4%. People showed up for affordable EVs. Supply showed up too. The market stopped looking like a fire sale.

What you buy is still not the Facebook post.

Checklist that keeps a 48-year-old and a 67-year-old out of trouble:

1) Battery state-of-health report. Not a guess. A number.
2) Remaining battery / bumper-to-bumper warranty in writing.
3) Level 2 home charging plan on day one (even a simple 120V overnight habit beats range panic).
4) Insurance quote before you fall in love.
5) Real winter range if you live where it snows. Cut the brochure number and live with it.

US kitchen-table take:

You do not need a brand-new $50k hatchback to quit the gas pump for school runs and grocery loops. You need a clean title, a healthy battery, and a plug at home. The depreciation already happened for someone else. That is the discount.

35-54 line: under $30k is where EV ownership stops being a TED Talk and starts being a payment.

55+ line: fewer oil changes, home charging, and a quieter driveway. Verify the battery like you would verify a heart report.

drafts.title: Illinois ~$300/kWh battery + 5-yr VPP
drafts.angle: Illinois utility battery rebate is real money: about $300 per kWh of storage (roughly $4,050 on a 13.5 kWh pack) through Dec 31, 2029. Since June 1, 2026 you take the rebate only if you join the utility scheduled-dispatch VPP. Five-year commitment. Kitchen-table move: stack the check, then ask what hours they can pull your battery.
bullets: Statute 220 ILCS 5/16-107.6: distributed storage base rebate $300 per kWh nameplate through Dec 31, 2029; $250/kWh after. Solar smart-inverter rebate separately $300/kW through 2029.
Typical 13.5 kWh home battery math used in trade explainers: ~$4,050 rebate before other incentives.
As of June 1, 2026 (Ameren DER Bulletin 2026-04 + ComEd practice): storage rebate requires Scheduled Dispatch VPP enrollment. Ameren: battery must be paired with solar for the storage rebate.

VPP: five-year dispatch commitment in statute. Weekday summer window talk often 4-6pm June-September once live. Statutory performance floor at least $10 per kW of average dispatch per program year on top of the upfront rebate.
Federal residential storage credit expired end of 2025. State/utility cash is the remaining lever for many Midwestern shoppers.
drafts.body:
Illinois just made the battery math loud.

If you put a home battery behind a smart inverter, the utility rebate is written into state law at $300 per kilowatt-hour of battery capacity through the end of 2029. On a common 13.5 kWh pack, that is about $4,050 before you stack anything else. The solar half of the smart-inverter rebate is $300 per kilowatt of panels.

That is the headline. Here is the catch most Facebook ads skip.

Since June 1, 2026, taking the storage rebate means joining your utility's Scheduled Dispatch Virtual Power Plant. Five years. They can call your battery on peak afternoons so your house leans on stored power instead of the grid. Ameren also wants the battery paired with solar for that storage rebate. ComEd adds a qualifying supply product for the life of the battery in their filed terms. Read your utility's packet, not a national blog.

You still get paid for showing up. Statute floors the performance pay at $10 per kW of average dispatch for the season, paid at year end, on top of the upfront check. It will not replace a Powerwall sticker by itself. It can knock a real chunk off the install invoice.

US kitchen-table take for a 45-year-old in the Chicago suburbs or a 58-year-old watching Medicare premiums climb:

This is not free money with no strings. It is a contract. The independence win is still real if you want backup lights and a quieter summer peak bill. The independence fail is signing before you know which hours they can pull, what reserve you keep for outages, and whether your rate plan changes.

Checklist before you wire the deposit:

1) Get the rebate dollar amount in writing for your exact kWh size.
2) Get the VPP hours, season, and early-exit rules in writing.
3) Ask what backup reserve you keep during events.
4) Confirm solar pairing rules if you are Ameren territory.
5) Compare the net after rebate to a smaller battery you actually need for fridge / CPAP / router, not a showroom full wall.

35-54 line: $4k off a battery is how middle-class households stop waiting for a federal credit that already ended.

55+ line: backup for medical devices and summer heat is the product. The rebate is just how you buy it without draining the emergency fund.

drafts.title: Colorado 10% battery tax credit clock
drafts.window: 8-11 AM MT Saturday (Colorado feed is awake).
drafts.angle: Colorado residential energy storage income-tax credit is 10% of purchase price for installs in tax years through 2026 (SB25-026 extended it before Jan 1, 2027). Form DR 1307. Unused credit generally does not refund or carry if you keep it yourself. Brian's state. Kitchen-table: get the install date inside the window or stop pretending "maybe next year."
bullets: CRS 39-22-546 (as amended by SB25-026): 10% of purchase price for qualifying residential energy storage installed for income tax years commencing on or after Jan 1, 2023 and before Jan 1, 2027.
Purchase price for the credit: hardware you paid the contractor/manufacturer; Colorado DR 1307 says include sales tax and freight, exclude permit/assembly/install labor.
If you keep the credit: amount over your tax due is generally not refunded and may not carry forward. Assignment to the seller can change that (assignee can get refund of excess).
Federal residential storage credit ended Dec 31, 2025. State 10% is one of the clean remaining Colorado levers alongside utility programs.
Brian context (do not overshare medical detail in post): rooftop solar already in; battery still a maybe. Clock is the story, not a sales pitch.
drafts.body:
Colorado put a date on the battery discount.

If you install a qualifying home battery in a Colorado house, the state income-tax credit is 10 percent of the purchase price for tax years that start before January 1, 2027. That is the window SB25-026 locked in. Miss the install timing and you are shopping without that 10%.

How the form works matters more than the slogan.

Colorado DR 1307 is the certification. Purchase price for the credit is what you paid for the battery hardware (they let you include sales tax and freight). Labor, permits, and "construction services" stay out of that line. Multiply by 10%. That is your credit.

If you claim it yourself and it is bigger than your Colorado tax bill, the leftover generally does not come back as a check and does not roll to next year. Some households assign the credit to the seller so the economics clear at closing. Ask your tax person before you sign a contract that assumes a refund you will never see.

Federal storage credit is already gone as of the end of 2025. So for a lot of Colorado roofs that already have panels, this 10% is one of the clean remaining levers. Utility rebates and VPP pay still matter. Stack them in writing. Do not stack them in your head.

Kitchen-table take for Western Slope and Front Range alike:

You do not need a TED Talk about chemistry. You need an install date that lands inside the credit year, a DR 1307 that matches the invoice, and a clear answer on assignment vs keeping the credit.

Independence checklist:

1) Ask the contractor for a written purchase-price line that matches DR 1307 rules.
2) Ask whether they will take an assignment of the credit.
3) Ask your utility what battery cash or VPP pay still stacks in your territory (Xcel medical/PSPS rules are a separate conversation).
4) If you are still "waiting for the next federal deal," price the Colorado 10% as money you leave on the table after Dec 2026 installs fall out of the window.

35-54 line: this is a calendar problem, not a gadget problem.

55+ line: backup for heat, CPAP, and fridge is the product. The 10% is how Colorado helps you buy it this year.

drafts.title: Oasis Supercharger: solar + batteries Labor Day
drafts.window: 8-11 AM MT Saturday (also late morning). Holiday-travel scrollers.
drafts.angle: Tesla Charging Sep 11, 2026: Oasis Supercharger in Lost Hills, CA posted Labor Day stats  -  6,038 sessions / 4 days / 164 stalls, ~11.2 sessions/stall Monday with zero waiters, ~7 MW on-site solar generated. Site: ~11 MW solar + 10 Megapacks (~39 MWh). Kitchen-table: solar+storage is how EV charging (and home backup) survives peak demand without wrecking the bill.
bullets: TeslaCharging Sep 11, 2026: Oasis Lost Hills Labor Day  -  6,038 sessions over 4 days across 164 stalls; Monday 11.2 sessions/stall; zero waiters.
About 7 MW of solar generated on-site during the holiday window (11 MW array + canopies designed into the project).
About 10 Megapacks / ~39 MWh storage lets the station ride through demand spikes and low sun.
World-scale Supercharger on the I-5 LA-SF corridor; built to run largely on local solar+storage rather than only the grid feeder.
US household lesson: pair generation with storage  -  same stack as a home solar+battery, just bigger.
drafts.body:
Labor Day just stress-tested solar-plus-battery charging on the busiest EV corridor in California.

Tesla Charging posted the Oasis Supercharger scoreboard for Lost Hills on Highway 46 / I-5: 6,038 sessions over four days across 164 stalls. Monday hit about 11.2 sessions per stall with zero waiters. On-site solar generated about 7 megawatts during that window. The site was built as an 11 MW solar farm plus canopies with 10 Megapacks (about 39 MWh of storage) so most of the station can run on local sun and batteries instead of yanking the neighborhood feeder every time a holiday convoy plugs in.

That is the clean-energy product in one picture.

You are not buying a Megapack for your garage. You are watching the same stack that belongs on a family roof and a town microgrid: make power when the sun is up, store it, use it when demand spikes. Road-trip charging that does not turn into a line is how EV ownership stops feeling fragile for a 40-year-old with kids in the back seat and a 65-year-old who only wants a quiet coffee stop.

US kitchen-table take:

1) Solar without storage is half a plan. Oasis works because the batteries eat the spike.
2) When utilities stall interconnects, sites that can mostly self-supply get built faster. Your home battery and rooftop math rhyme with that.
3) Ask your utility what they are building for peak days: wires, storage, or both. Cheap generation that cannot move is how bills climb.

35-54 line: this is why you pair panels with a battery instead of waiting for the perfect federal credit.

55+ line: independence on the highway looks like no queue. Independence at home looks like a fridge that stays cold.

Extremely pro solar. Extremely pro batteries. Extremely pro EVs that actually charge when families travel.
